---
title: "CEBR 3D Catchment"
author: "ROSSyndicate"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

This R markdown builds 3D views of CEBR's Blowhard Spring water supply from the
elevatr DEM, with vertical exaggeration and either draped aerial imagery or a 
shaded-relief texture. 

Rendering uses {rayshader}. On macOS, {rgl} and {rayrender} need XQuartz
(<https://www.xquartz.org>) to load, even when no window is opened. Install it
once (`brew install --cask xquartz`, then log out and back in).

# 1. Setup

```{r setup}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE,
                      message = FALSE,
                      warning = FALSE,
                      eval = TRUE)

knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())

source("setup.R")

# Render off-screen by default. Set TRUE for a live window you can rotate by
# hand; this needs XQuartz running (log out and back in after installing it),
# otherwise rgl crashes the R session when it opens the window. Restart R after
# changing it, since rgl reads this option when it loads.
open_window <- FALSE
options(rgl.useNULL = !open_window)
library(rayshader)

```

```{r nps_basemaps}


# NPS Park Tiles basemap helpers used by the MORA WSVA figures.
# Sourced automatically by setup.R (all files in src/).

#' Download the NPS Park Tiles basemap for an area
#'
#' Park Tiles is the National Park Service's own basemap
#' (https://www.nps.gov/maps/tools/park-tiles/). NPS serves it from its Atlas
#' tile server; the style IDs and public access token below come from NPS's
#' map library (npmap.js 4.2.1, the code behind the Park Tiles viewer). If NPS
#' rotates the token, update `nps_token` from
#' https://www.nps.gov/lib/npmap.js/4.2.1/npmap.min.js (search "atlas-user").
#'
#' @param aoi sf object to cover, e.g. from `getParkBoundary()`.
#' @param style `"standard"`, `"light"` or `"slate"`.
#' @param buffer_km Margin around `aoi`, in km.
#' @param zoom Tile zoom level, or `NULL` to let maptiles choose.
#'
#' @return A SpatRaster (RGB, Web Mercator) for `geom_nps_basemap()`.
get_nps_basemap <- function(aoi, style = "standard", buffer_km = 2, zoom = NULL){

  style_ids <- c(standard = "ck58pyquo009v01p99xebegr9",
                 light = "ck5cpia2u0auf01p9vbugvcpv",
                 slate = "ck5cpvc2e0avf01p9zaw4co8o")
  nps_token <- get_nps_tiles_token()  # read at run time (src/nps_basemap.R)

  # maptiles detects the image type from ".png" in the URL. The server rejects
  # extra query parameters, so ".png" goes in a URL fragment, which curl never
  # sends.
  provider <- maptiles::create_provider(
    name = paste0("nps_park_tiles_", style),
    url = paste0("https://atlas-stg.geoplatform.gov/styles/v1/atlas-user/",
                 style_ids[[style]], "/tiles/256/{z}/{x}/{y}?access_token=", nps_token,
                 "#.png"),
    citation = "NPS Park Tiles; (c) Mapbox (c) OpenStreetMap contributors"
  )

  # Tiles come back in the CRS of `area`; Web Mercator is their native CRS, so
  # no resampling, and it matches coord_sf(crs = 3857) in the plot.
  area <- sf::st_buffer(sf::st_union(sf::st_transform(aoi, 4326)), buffer_km * 1000) %>%
    sf::st_transform(3857) %>%
    sf::st_as_sf()

  if (is.null(zoom)) {
    maptiles::get_tiles(area, provider = provider, crop = TRUE)
  } else {
    maptiles::get_tiles(area, provider = provider, zoom = zoom, crop = TRUE)
  }
}


#' ggplot layer for a basemap from `get_nps_basemap()`
#'
#' Draws the tiles as a background image, so other layers keep their own fill
#' and color scales. Add `coord_sf(crs = 3857)` to the plot, since the tiles
#' are in Web Mercator.
#'
#' @param tiles SpatRaster from `get_nps_basemap()`.
geom_nps_basemap <- function(tiles){

  rgb <- terra::as.array(tiles[[1:3]]) / 255
  e <- terra::ext(tiles)

  annotation_raster(grDevices::as.raster(rgb),
                    xmin = e$xmin, xmax = e$xmax, ymin = e$ymin, ymax = e$ymax)
}


#' Use NPS Park Tiles as the basemaps of a mapview or leaflet map
#'
#' Replaces mapview's default basemaps (CartoDB, OpenStreetMap, ...) with the
#' four Park Tiles styles and rebuilds the layer switcher, keeping the map's
#' own layers as toggleable overlays.
#'
#' @param m A mapview object (e.g. `mapview(a) + mapview(b)`) or leaflet map.
#' @param styles Park Tiles styles to offer, first one shown by default.
#'
#' @return The same kind of object as `m`.
add_nps_basemaps <- function(m, styles = c("standard", "light", "slate", "imagery")){

  style_ids <- c(standard = "ck58pyquo009v01p99xebegr9",
                 light = "ck5cpia2u0auf01p9vbugvcpv",
                 slate = "ck5cpvc2e0avf01p9zaw4co8o",
                 imagery = "ck72fwp2642dv07o7tbqinvz4")
  nps_token <- get_nps_tiles_token()  # read at run time (src/nps_basemap.R)

  lm <- if (inherits(m, "mapview")) m@map else m

  # Keep the overlay names from the existing layer switcher, then drop
  # mapview's basemaps and that switcher.
  calls <- lm$x$calls
  control <- Filter(function(cl) cl$method == "addLayersControl", calls)
  overlays <- if (length(control) > 0) unlist(control[[length(control)]]$args[[2]]) else character(0)
  lm$x$calls <- Filter(function(cl) !cl$method %in% c("addProviderTiles", "addTiles", "addLayersControl"), calls)

  group_names <- paste("NPS", tools::toTitleCase(styles))

  for (i in rev(seq_along(styles))) {
    lm <- leaflet::addTiles(
      lm,
      urlTemplate = paste0("https://atlas-stg.geoplatform.gov/styles/v1/atlas-user/",
                           style_ids[[styles[i]]], "/tiles/256/{z}/{x}/{y}?access_token=", nps_token),
      attribution = "NPS Park Tiles | &copy; Mapbox &copy; OpenStreetMap contributors",
      group = group_names[i]
    )
  }

  # Show only the first style at start so the others don't load until picked.
  lm <- leaflet::addLayersControl(lm, baseGroups = group_names, overlayGroups = overlays,
                                  options = leaflet::layersControlOptions(collapsed = TRUE)) %>%
    leaflet::hideGroup(group_names[-1])

  if (inherits(m, "mapview")) {
    m@map <- lm
    m
  } else {
    lm
  }
}



```


## - Figure settings

Everything that controls the look of the figures is set here.

```{r settings}

# Vertical exaggeration (1 = true relief). 2 reads well for this relief.
z_exag <- 2

# Lidar is 1.5 ft; aggregate by this factor for rendering (6 -> 9 ft cells).
# Lower for more detail, at the cost of memory and render time.
dem_agg <- 6

# Buffer around the Paradise River catchment for the basin view (ft)
aoi_buffer_ft <- 5000

# Surface texture: "imagery" (Esri World Imagery) or "hillshade" or "nps"
drape <- "hillshade" #"hillshade"

# Catchment styling: outline width (texture pixels) and fill opacity. The
# catchments are nested, so the fill deepens toward Edith Current.
outline_width <- 2
fill_alpha <- 0.3

# Imagery tile zoom (16 is ~2 m per pixel at this latitude)
imagery_zoom <- 16

# Camera for the basin view: theta = compass direction the camera sits on,
# measured as rotation around the scene (0 = looking north from the south),
# phi = elevation angle above the horizon, zoom < 1 moves in.
cam_basin <- list(theta = -325, phi = 45, zoom = 0.75, fov = 40)
cam_mountain <- list(theta = 15, phi = 25, zoom = 0.65, fov = 40)

# Preview mode: TRUE shows a quick low-sample render at half size in the plot
# pane instead of the full path-traced figure, for tuning the camera. Set FALSE for
# the final figures.
preview <- TRUE

# Output size (px) and path tracer samples for render_highquality()
out_width <- 2200
out_height <- 1800
hq_samples <- 256

# Visitor center and roads. The visitor center footprint is smaller than a DEM
# cell at this scale, so it is drawn as a circle marker of this radius (m).
show_visitor_center <- TRUE
visitor_center_color <- "#ffd400"
visitor_center_radius_m <- 200
show_roads      <- TRUE
# Test well and Blowhard Mountain Radar weather station markers (draped on the
# terrain; the well is a circle, the station a square), sized in metres
show_test_well <- TRUE
test_well_color <- "#1f78b4"
show_weather_station <- TRUE
weather_station_color <- "#252525"
site_marker_radius_m <- 150
# OpenStreetMap road classes to draw: main roads only (SR-148, SR-143, Cedar
# Canyon Road); add "tertiary", "service", etc. for more detail
road_types <- c("primary", "secondary")
road_color <- "gray72"
road_casing <- FALSE   # TRUE adds a white edge under the roads
park_boundary_color <- "#1b7a4a"
park_boundary_width <- 6

# Scale bar, drawn on the terrain along one edge of the model ("N", "S", "E",
# or "W") and true to scale where it is drawn.
# Put it on an edge facing the camera: with cam_basin theta = -145, north is
# toward the lower right of the image, so the N edge is in front.
scalebar_km       <- 5
scalebar_position <- "N"
scalebar_start    <- 0.10   # where the bar starts along that edge (fraction)
scalebar_inset    <- 0.05   # how far in from the edge the bar sits (fraction)
# Nudge the drawn bar on the image (fraction of image width, height; +x right,
# +y down), e.g. c(0.03, 0.05) to move it off the block onto the white
# background. Length and angle stay as measured on the terrain.
scalebar_shift    <- c(0., 0.05)

# North arrow, drawn on the image and rotated to where north points in this
# view. Position is a fraction of the image width / height from the top left.
north_arrow_x <- 0.06
north_arrow_y <- 0.62

# Elevation color bar (hillshade drape only), drawn in the white space at the
# right of the render. Uses the same palette as the hypsometric tint.
show_elevation_bar <- TRUE
elev_bar_x <- 0.90   # center of the bar (fraction of image width)
elev_bar_y <- c(0.38, 0.64)   # top and bottom (fractions of image height)
hypso_colors <- c("#b86b43", "#d9a56c", "#d1c29e", "#8da173", "#3b5c36", "white")

# Catchment colors match the other report figures
system_colors <- c(
  "Blowhard Recharge Area"   = "hotpink",
  #"Blowhard Intake"          = "hotpink",
  "Cedar Breaks Boundary"  = park_boundary_color,
  "Faults"                   = "#252525",
  "Springs"                  = "hotpink",
  "Visitor Center"         = visitor_center_color,
  "Test Well"              = test_well_color,
  "Weather Station"        = weather_station_color,
  "Roads"                  = road_color
)

# Callout boxes configuration (box_x / box_y are fractions from top-left)
callouts <- tibble::tribble(
  ~system,                 ~label,            ~box_x, ~box_y, ~aim_x, ~aim_y,
  "Blowhard Intake",       "Blowhard Intake",  0.80,   0.2,   NA,     NA,
  "Cedar Breaks Boundary", "Cedar Breaks",  0.25,   0.20,   NA,     NA,
  "Visitor Center",        "Visitor Center",  0.55,   0.10,   NA,     NA,
  "Test Well",             "Test Well",       0.70,   0.08,   NA,     NA,
  "Weather Station",       "Blowhard Mtn. Radar\nWeather Station", 0.88, 0.29, NA, NA
)

# Text size for all labels on the figure (callouts, scale bar, elevation bar,
# legend, and notes), as a cex at the 2400 px reference width
text_cex <- 3

# Legend: a boxed, stacked list drawn on the image. `legend_corner` is the
# box's bottom-right corner (fraction of image width, height from top left).
# List names in `legend_drop` to leave items out, e.g. ones already named by a
# callout: c("Cedar Breaks Boundary", "Visitor Center")
legend_corner <- c(0.98, 0.98)
legend_drop <- character(0)

# White band added above the render to hold the callouts (fraction of the
# render height). Set to 0 if the camera already leaves enough sky.
callout_band <- 0.0


fig_dir <- "data/park/CEBR/Figs"

```

# 2. Catchments, streams, and outlets

Same catchment files as `MORA_Deep_Dive_workflow.Rmd`. The lidar DTM is in
Washington State Plane South (US ft), which is close to north-up here, so the
vectors are projected to the DEM rather than the other way around.

```{r vectors}


# --- 1. Load and Filter Water Supply Database ---
table_path <- "data/Water_Supply_Systems/NPS_Water_Systems_Database_Joined.xlsx"

# Import database, filter to CEBR, and convert to spatial (sf) object
blowhard_spring <- read_excel(table_path, sheet = 1, na = c("NA", "U"), skip = 1) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    park_unit   == "CEBR",
    !source_type %in% c("hauled", "Hauled")
  ) %>%
  drop_na(source_longitude, source_latitude) %>%
  st_as_sf(
    coords = c("source_longitude", "source_latitude"),
    crs    = 4326,
    remove = FALSE
  )

park_boundary <- readRDS("data/park/CEBR/report_data/park_boundary.rds")


# --- In Chunk 2: vectors ---
dem_path <- "data/park/CEBR/report_data/park_dem.tif"

if (file.exists(dem_path)) {
  dem <- terra::rast(dem_path)
} else {
  dem_raw <- elevatr::get_elev_raster(park_boundary %>% sf::st_buffer(aoi_buffer_ft), z = 14) %>% 
    terra::rast()
  dem <- terra::project(dem_raw, "EPSG:32612")
  terra::writeRaster(dem, dem_path, overwrite = TRUE)
}

# Ensure dem is in UTM meters
if (terra::is.lonlat(dem)) {
  dem <- terra::project(dem, "EPSG:32612")
}
dem_crs <- terra::crs(dem)


catchments <- readRDS("data/park/CEBR/Climate_Data/recharge_area.rds") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(system = "Blowhard Recharge Area") %>%
  dplyr::filter(!sf::st_is_empty(.)) %>%    # <--- Remove empty geometries
  dplyr::select(system) %>%
  sf::st_transform(dem_crs) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(system = factor(system, levels = names(system_colors)))

streams <- readRDS("data/park/CEBR/report_data/park_flowlines.rds") %>%
  sf::st_transform(dem_crs)

# Outlets: the existing Edith Creek intake (water system database) and the
# snapped pour points used to delineate the two downstream catchments
current_intake <- blowhard_spring %>%
  sf::st_transform(dem_crs) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(system = "Blowhard Recharge Area")


springs_joined <- readRDS("data/park/CEBR/report_data/springs_joined.rds") %>%
  st_transform(dem_crs)

# 1. Force all vector layers to match the exact DEM CRS
catchments <- catchments %>% sf::st_transform(dem_crs)
streams <- streams %>% sf::st_transform(dem_crs)
park_boundary <- park_boundary %>% sf::st_transform(dem_crs)


#springs_joined_elev <- elevatr::get_elev_point(springs_joined)

# Geology
nps_gdb   <- "data/park/CEBR/cebr_geology_gdb/cebr_geology.gdb"
nps_faults <- st_read(nps_gdb, layer = "cebrflt") %>% 
  sf::st_transform(dem_crs)

# Visitor center (from the NPS building footprints), drawn at its centroid
visitor_center <- readRDS("data/park/CEBR/report_data/buildings.rds") %>%
  dplyr::filter(BLDGNAME == "Visitor Center") %>%
  st_transform(dem_crs) %>%
  st_centroid() %>%
  dplyr::transmute(system = "Visitor Center")

# Roads from OpenStreetMap, cached so Overpass is only queried once
roads_path <- "data/park/CEBR/report_data/osm_roads.rds"
if (file.exists(roads_path)) {
  roads <- readRDS(roads_path)
} else {
  roads_bbox <- park_boundary %>%
    sf::st_buffer(aoi_buffer_ft) %>%
    sf::st_transform(4326) %>%
    sf::st_bbox()
  # Overpass servers are often busy (HTTP 429/502), so try a mirror if needed
  for (url in c("https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter",
                "https://overpass.kumi.systems/api/interpreter")) {
    osmdata::set_overpass_url(url)
    roads <- tryCatch(
      osmdata::opq(bbox = as.numeric(roads_bbox), timeout = 120) %>%
        osmdata::add_osm_feature(key = "highway") %>%
        osmdata::osmdata_sf() %>%
        purrr::pluck("osm_lines") %>%
        dplyr::select(osm_id, name, highway),
      error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(roads)) break
  }
  if (is.null(roads)) stop("Could not download OSM roads; try again later.")
  saveRDS(roads, roads_path)
}
roads <- roads %>%
  dplyr::filter(highway %in% road_types) %>%
  sf::st_transform(dem_crs)

# Test well
test_well <- data.frame(
  name = c("Test Well Log"),
  lat = c(37.607578),
  lon = c(-112.846386),
  WIN = c(25797),
  WRCHEX = c("73-424")
) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(dem_crs) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(system = "Test Well")


# blowhard mountain radar weather station
blowhard_station <- readRDS( "data/park/CEBR/report_data/blowhard_station.rds") %>%
  st_transform(dem_crs) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(name, system = "Weather Station")

```

# 3. Helper functions

`drape_texture()` builds the surface texture for a DEM, and `add_catchments()`
adds the catchment outlines, streams, and outlets on top. Outlines get a white
halo so they read on both imagery and shaded relief.

```{r helpers}

# Esri World Imagery tiles warped onto the DEM grid, as an RGB array in [0, 1]
get_imagery <- function(dem, zoom) {
  aoi <- sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(dem)) %>%
    sf::st_transform(4326)
  tiles <- maptiles::get_tiles(aoi, provider = "Esri.WorldImagery",
                               zoom = zoom, crop = TRUE)
  img <- terra::project(tiles[[1:3]], dem, method = "bilinear")
  arr <- terra::as.array(img) / 255
  arr[is.na(arr)] <- 0
  pmin(pmax(arr, 0), 1)
}


drape_texture <- function(dem, elmat, drape, zscale, zoom = 16) {
  shadow <- ray_shade(elmat, zscale = zscale, sunaltitude = 35,
                      sunangle = 225, multicore = TRUE)
  ambient <- ambient_shade(elmat, zscale = zscale, multicore = TRUE)
  
  if (drape %in% c("imagery", "nps", "light", "slate", "standard")) {
    # Choose style based on drape argument or default to "standard"
    style_choice <- if (drape %in% c("standard", "light", "slate")) drape else "standard"
    
    get_nps_texture(dem, dem_crs, style = style_choice, zoom = zoom) %>%
      add_shadow(shadow, max_darken = 0.4) %>%
      add_shadow(ambient, max_darken = 0.2)
  } else {
    # Muted hypsometric tint fallback
    hypso <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(hypso_colors)(256)
    elmat %>%
      height_shade(texture = hypso) %>%
      add_shadow(lamb_shade(elmat, zscale = zscale, sunangle = 225), 0.3) %>%
      add_shadow(shadow, max_darken = 0.5) %>%
      add_shadow(ambient, max_darken = 0.2)
  }
}


add_catchments <- function(texture, elmat, extent, line_scale = 1) {
  out <- texture
  
  # Ensure extent is passed in a format rayshader natively accepts (sf bbox)
  if (inherits(extent, "SpatExtent")) {
    extent <- sf::st_bbox(c(
      xmin = extent[1], xmax = extent[2],
      ymin = extent[3], ymax = extent[4]
    ))
  }
  
  # Park Boundary
  if (exists("park_boundary") && nrow(park_boundary) > 0) {
    park_edge <- sf::st_cast(sf::st_boundary(park_boundary), "MULTILINESTRING")
    out <- out %>%
      add_overlay(generate_line_overlay(
        park_edge, extent = extent, heightmap = elmat,
        color = park_boundary_color,
        linewidth = park_boundary_width * line_scale
      ))
  }
  
  # Streams
  out <- add_overlay(out, generate_line_overlay(
    streams, extent = extent, heightmap = elmat,
    color = "#9fd3ff", 
    linewidth = 2 * line_scale))

  # Roads: a light gray line, optionally over a white casing
  if (show_roads && exists("roads") && nrow(roads) > 0) {
    if (road_casing) {
      out <- add_overlay(out, generate_line_overlay(
        roads, extent = extent, heightmap = elmat,
        color = "white", linewidth = 4.5 * line_scale))
    }
    out <- add_overlay(out, generate_line_overlay(
      roads, extent = extent, heightmap = elmat,
      color = road_color, linewidth = 2.5 * line_scale))
  }
  
  # Catchments  
  for (s in rev(levels(catchments$system))) {
    poly <- dplyr::filter(catchments, system == s)
    if (nrow(poly) == 0 || all(sf::st_is_empty(poly))) next
    
    edge <- sf::st_cast(poly, "MULTILINESTRING")
    if (nrow(edge) == 0 || all(sf::st_is_empty(edge))) next
    
    out <- out %>%
      add_overlay(generate_polygon_overlay(poly, extent = extent, heightmap = elmat,
                                           palette = system_colors[[s]],
                                           linecolor = NA),
                  alphalayer = fill_alpha) %>%
      add_overlay(generate_line_overlay(edge, extent = extent, heightmap = elmat,
                                        color = "white",
                                        linewidth = (outline_width + 3) * line_scale)) %>%
      add_overlay(generate_line_overlay(edge, extent = extent, heightmap = elmat,
                                        color = system_colors[[s]],
                                        linewidth = outline_width * line_scale))
  }
  
  # 5. Add Faults (Dark dashed/solid lines)
  if (exists("nps_faults") && nrow(nps_faults) > 0) {
    out <- out %>%
      # add_overlay(generate_line_overlay(
      #  nps_faults, extent = extent, heightmap = elmat,
      #  color = "white", # Dark charcoal / black for high contrast
      #  linewidth = 3 * line_scale
      #)) %>%
      add_overlay(generate_line_overlay(
        nps_faults, extent = extent, heightmap = elmat,
        color = "#252525", # Dark charcoal / black for high contrast
        linewidth = 4 * line_scale
      ))
  }
  
   # 3. Add Spring Elevation Emergence Band (Shaded Polygon)
  #if (exists("spring_band_sf") && nrow(spring_band_sf) > 0) {
  #  out <- out %>%
  #    add_overlay(generate_polygon_overlay(
  #      spring_band_sf, extent = extent, heightmap = elmat,
  #      palette = "hotpink", linecolor = "hotpink", linewidth = 1.5 * line_scale
  #    ), alphalayer = 0) # Adjust transparency here (0 to 1)
  #}
  
  # 4. Add Springs (Blue Circles)
  if (exists("springs_joined") && nrow(springs_joined) > 0) {
    springs_buffered <- sf::st_buffer(springs_joined, dist = 75) # 25 ft/m circle buffer
    out <- add_overlay(out, generate_polygon_overlay(
      springs_buffered, extent = extent, heightmap = elmat,
      palette = "hotpink", linecolor = "white", linewidth = 1.5 * line_scale
    ))
  }

  # 5. Add Current Intake Point (Gold / Red Circle)
  if (exists("current_intake") && nrow(current_intake) > 0) {
    intake_buffered <- sf::st_buffer(current_intake, dist = 75) # slightly larger circle
    out <- add_overlay(out, generate_polygon_overlay(
      intake_buffered, extent = extent, heightmap = elmat,
      palette = "hotpink", linecolor = "white", linewidth = 2 * line_scale
    ))
  }
  
  # Visitor center (yellow circle with a dark outline)
  if (show_visitor_center && exists("visitor_center") && nrow(visitor_center) > 0) {
    vc_buffered <- sf::st_buffer(visitor_center, dist = visitor_center_radius_m)
    out <- out %>%
      add_overlay(generate_polygon_overlay(
        vc_buffered, extent = extent, heightmap = elmat,
        palette = visitor_center_color, linecolor = "gray15",
        linewidth = 1.5 * line_scale
      ))
  }

  # Test well (circle) and weather station (square), white outlines
  if (show_test_well && exists("test_well") && nrow(test_well) > 0) {
    out <- add_overlay(out, generate_polygon_overlay(
      sf::st_buffer(test_well, dist = site_marker_radius_m),
      extent = extent, heightmap = elmat,
      palette = test_well_color, linecolor = "white", linewidth = 2 * line_scale
    ))
  }
  if (show_weather_station && exists("blowhard_station") && nrow(blowhard_station) > 0) {
    out <- add_overlay(out, generate_polygon_overlay(
      sf::st_buffer(blowhard_station, dist = site_marker_radius_m,
                    endCapStyle = "SQUARE"),
      extent = extent, heightmap = elmat,
      palette = weather_station_color, linecolor = "white", linewidth = 2 * line_scale
    ))
  }
 
  return(out)
}

# Candidate leader-line targets: points along each catchment outline, dropping
# stretches within `shared_ft` of a smaller catchment's outline. The nested
# catchments share parts of their ridges, and the smaller one is drawn on top,
# so those stretches show in the smaller catchment's color.
# Candidate leader-line targets: points along each catchment outline, dropping
# stretches within `shared_ft` of a smaller catchment's outline.
# Candidate leader-line targets: points along each catchment outline, dropping
# stretches within `shared_ft` of a smaller catchment's outline.
outline_points <- function(spacing_ft = 30, shared_ft = 60) {
  
  # Ensure catchments are in a projected CRS for st_line_sample()
  proj_catchments <- catchments
  original_crs <- sf::st_crs(catchments)
  
  if (sf::st_is_longlat(proj_catchments)) {
    # Transform to UTM Zone 12N (EPSG:32612 covers Cedar Breaks / Utah region)
    proj_catchments <- sf::st_transform(proj_catchments, 32612)
  }
  
  edge <- function(s) {
    proj_catchments %>%
      dplyr::filter(system %in% s) %>%
      sf::st_geometry() %>%
      sf::st_boundary() %>%
      sf::st_cast("LINESTRING", warn = FALSE)
  }
  
  lv <- levels(proj_catchments$system)   # smallest first
  
  sampled_pts <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(lv), function(i) {
    s <- lv[i]
    lines <- edge(s)
    
    # Sample points along the linestrings
    pts <- sf::st_line_sample(lines, density = 1 / spacing_ft)
    pts <- sf::st_cast(pts[!sf::st_is_empty(pts)], "POINT")
    
    keep <- rep(TRUE, length(pts))
    if (i > 1) {
      keep <- as.numeric(sf::st_distance(pts, edge(lv[seq_len(i - 1)]))) > shared_ft
    }
    sf::st_sf(system = s, geometry = pts[keep])
  })
  
  # Transform back to the original CRS so it matches the rest of your workflow
  sf::st_transform(sampled_pts, original_crs)
}

# Position of map points in the rendered image (fractions of width and height
# from the top left). Uses rayshader's scene coordinates (x = DEM column and
# z = DEM row, both centered; y = elevation / zscale) and the current rgl
# camera, which render_highquality() and render_snapshot() also use.
project_to_image <- function(pts, dem, zscale) {
  xy <- sf::st_coordinates(pts)[, 1:2, drop = FALSE]
  cell <- terra::res(dem)[1]
  elev <- terra::extract(dem, xy)[, 1]
  scene <- cbind((xy[, 1] - terra::xmin(dem)) / cell - terra::ncol(dem) / 2,
                 elev / zscale,
                 (terra::ymax(dem) - xy[, 2]) / cell - terra::nrow(dem) / 2)
  m <- rgl::par3d(c("modelMatrix", "projMatrix"))
  h <- cbind(scene, 1) %*% t(m$projMatrix %*% m$modelMatrix)
  data.frame(fx = (h[, 1] / h[, 4] + 1) / 2,
             fy = 1 - (h[, 2] / h[, 4] + 1) / 2)
}

# Callout boxes with leader lines drawn onto a rendered image. `targets` are
# outline points with their image positions (fx, fy); each box connects to the
# target of its catchment closest to the box.
add_callouts <- function(png_in, png_out, targets, band = callout_band) {
  img <- magick::image_read(png_in)
  info <- magick::image_info(img)
  w <- info$width
  pad <- round(band * info$height)
  if (pad > 0) {
    img <- magick::image_append(c(magick::image_blank(w, pad, "white"), img),
                                stack = TRUE)
  }
  h <- info$height + pad
  s <- w / 2400
  img <- magick::image_draw(img)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(callouts))) {
    col <- "black"#system_colors[[callouts$system[i]]]
    bx <- callouts$box_x[i] * w
    by <- callouts$box_y[i] * h
    tg <- dplyr::filter(targets, system == callouts$system[i], !is.na(fx))
    if (nrow(tg) == 0) next   # feature turned off or outside the model
    tx <- tg$fx * w
    ty <- tg$fy * info$height + pad
    aim_x <- dplyr::coalesce(callouts$aim_x[i], callouts$box_x[i]) * w
    aim_y <- dplyr::coalesce(callouts$aim_y[i], callouts$box_y[i]) * h
    j <- which.min((tx - aim_x)^2 + (ty - aim_y)^2)
    cex <- text_cex * s
    # image_draw() flips the y axis, so text heights come back negative
    half_w <- abs(strwidth(callouts$label[i], cex = cex, font = 2)) / 2 + 28 * s
    half_h <- abs(strheight(callouts$label[i], cex = cex, font = 2)) / 2 + 20 * s
    # Leader starts at the point on the box edge closest to its target
    sx <- min(max(tx[j], bx - half_w), bx + half_w)
    sy <- min(max(ty[j], by - half_h), by + half_h)
    #segments(sx, sy, tx[j], ty[j], col = "white", lwd = 7 * s)
    segments(sx, sy, tx[j], ty[j], col = col, lwd = 3.5 * s)
    points(tx[j], ty[j], pch = 21, bg = col, col = "white", cex = 2.2 * s, lwd = 3 * s)
    rect(bx - half_w, by - half_h, bx + half_w, by + half_h,
         col = "white", border = col, lwd = 4 * s)
    text(bx, by, callouts$label[i], cex = cex, font = 2, col = "gray15")
  }
  dev.off()
  magick::image_write(img, png_out)
  png_out
}

# Ground points for the scale bar: `scalebar_km` along the `scalebar_position`
# edge, `scalebar_inset` in from it, with a tick at every quarter. Points are on
# the terrain surface, so the bar is true to scale where it is drawn.
scalebar_ground_points <- function(dem) {
  e <- terra::ext(dem)
  w <- e$xmax - e$xmin; h <- e$ymax - e$ymin
  d <- seq(0, scalebar_km * 1000, length.out = 5)   # metres along the bar
  xy <- switch(scalebar_position,
    N = cbind(e$xmin + scalebar_start * w + d, e$ymax - scalebar_inset * h),
    S = cbind(e$xmin + scalebar_start * w + d, e$ymin + scalebar_inset * h),
    E = cbind(e$xmax - scalebar_inset * w, e$ymin + scalebar_start * h + d),
    W = cbind(e$xmin + scalebar_inset * w, e$ymin + scalebar_start * h + d))
  sf::st_as_sf(data.frame(km = d / 1000, x = xy[, 1], y = xy[, 2]),
               coords = c("x", "y"), crs = terra::crs(dem))
}

# Draws the projected scale bar (alternating dark and white segments with km
# labels) onto a rendered image. `pts` has km, fx, fy from project_to_image().
add_scalebar <- function(png_in, png_out, pts) {
  img <- magick::image_read(png_in)
  info <- magick::image_info(img)
  w <- info$width; h <- info$height
  s <- w / 2400
  px <- (pts$fx + scalebar_shift[1]) * w; py <- (pts$fy + scalebar_shift[2]) * h
  img <- magick::image_draw(img)
  # dark outline, then alternating dark and white segments
  segments(px[1], py[1], px[length(px)], py[length(py)], col = "gray10", lwd = 26 * s, lend = 1)
  for (i in seq_len(length(px) - 1)) {
    segments(px[i], py[i], px[i + 1], py[i + 1],
             col = if (i %% 2 == 1) "gray10" else "white", lwd = 18 * s, lend = 1)
  }
  # Labels sit just off the bar on its upper (terrain) side, with a white halo
  # so they read over shaded relief
  u <- c(px[length(px)] - px[1], py[length(py)] - py[1]); u <- u / sqrt(sum(u^2))
  n <- c(-u[2], u[1]); if (n[2] > 0) n <- -n
  lab <- c(0, scalebar_km / 2, scalebar_km)
  idx <- c(1, ceiling(length(px) / 2), length(px))
  lx <- px[idx] + n[1] * 60 * s; ly <- py[idx] + n[2] * 60 * s
  labels <- c(lab[1:2], paste(lab[3], "km"))
  for (a in seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 13)) {
    text(lx + cos(a) * 4 * s, ly + sin(a) * 4 * s, labels = labels,
         cex = text_cex * s, font = 2, col = "white")
  }
  text(lx, ly, labels = labels, cex = text_cex * s, font = 2, col = "gray10")
  dev.off()
  magick::image_write(img, png_out)
  png_out
}

# Two ground points one km apart (south to north) at the DEM center; their
# image positions give the direction north points in the rendered view.
north_ground_points <- function(dem) {
  e <- terra::ext(dem)
  cx <- (e$xmin + e$xmax) / 2; cy <- (e$ymin + e$ymax) / 2
  sf::st_as_sf(data.frame(x = c(cx, cx), y = c(cy, cy + 1000)),
               coords = c("x", "y"), crs = terra::crs(dem))
}

# Plain north arrow (half black, half white) drawn on the image, rotated to
# match the projected north direction. `npx` has fx, fy for the two points
# from north_ground_points().
add_north_arrow <- function(png_in, png_out, npx) {
  img <- magick::image_read(png_in)
  info <- magick::image_info(img); w <- info$width; h <- info$height
  s <- w / 2400
  v <- c((npx$fx[2] - npx$fx[1]) * w, (npx$fy[2] - npx$fy[1]) * h)
  v <- v / sqrt(sum(v^2))                # unit vector pointing north (image)
  p <- c(-v[2], v[1])                    # perpendicular
  cx <- north_arrow_x * w; cy <- north_arrow_y * h
  L <- 110 * s; W <- 38 * s
  tip <- c(cx, cy) + v * L; tail <- c(cx, cy) - v * L * 0.55
  left <- tail + p * W; right <- tail - p * W
  img <- magick::image_draw(img)
  polygon(c(tip[1], left[1], cx), c(tip[2], left[2], cy), col = "gray10", border = "gray10", lwd = 2 * s)
  polygon(c(tip[1], right[1], cx), c(tip[2], right[2], cy), col = "white", border = "gray10", lwd = 2 * s)
  lab <- tip + v * 42 * s
  text(lab[1], lab[2], "N", cex = 1.1 * text_cex * s, font = 2, col = "gray10")
  dev.off()
  magick::image_write(img, png_out)
  png_out
}

# Vertical elevation color bar matching the hypsometric tint (which spans the
# basin DEM's elevation range), labeled in feet.
add_elevation_bar <- function(png_in, png_out, elev_range_m) {
  img <- magick::image_read(png_in)
  info <- magick::image_info(img); w <- info$width; h <- info$height
  s <- w / 2400
  cols <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(hypso_colors)(256)
  x0 <- elev_bar_x * w - 22 * s; x1 <- elev_bar_x * w + 22 * s
  ytop <- elev_bar_y[1] * h; ybot <- elev_bar_y[2] * h
  yy <- seq(ybot, ytop, length.out = length(cols) + 1)
  rng_ft <- elev_range_m * 3.28084
  ticks <- pretty(rng_ft, n = 5); ticks <- ticks[ticks >= rng_ft[1] & ticks <= rng_ft[2]]
  img <- magick::image_draw(img)
  rect(x0, yy[-length(yy)], x1, yy[-1], col = cols, border = NA)
  rect(x0, ytop, x1, ybot, border = "gray20", lwd = 2 * s)
  ty <- ybot + (ticks - rng_ft[1]) / diff(rng_ft) * (ytop - ybot)
  # ticks and labels on the right, away from the block
  segments(x1, ty, x1 + 10 * s, ty, col = "gray20", lwd = 2 * s)
  text(x1 + 16 * s, ty, format(ticks, big.mark = ","), adj = c(0, 0.5),
       cex = text_cex * s, col = "gray15")
  text(elev_bar_x * w + 50 * s, ytop - 55 * s, "Elevation (ft)", cex = text_cex * s, font = 2, col = "gray15")
  dev.off()
  magick::image_write(img, png_out)
  png_out
}

# Boxed, stacked legend drawn on the render, plus the exaggeration note and
# data credits in a strip below it
add_legend <- function(png_in, png_out, credit) {
  img <- magick::image_read(png_in)
  info <- magick::image_info(img); w <- info$width; h <- info$height
  s <- w / 2400
  cex <- text_cex * s

  # Explicit legend items to display
  legend_items <- list(
    list(name = "Blowhard Recharge Area", color = "hotpink", type = "fill"),
    #list(name = "Blowhard Intake",         color = "hotpink", type = "point"),
    list(name = "Cedar Breaks Boundary",   color = park_boundary_color, type = "line"),
    list(name = "Faults",                  color = "#252525", type = "line"),
    list(name = "Springs",                 color = "hotpink", type = "point"),
    list(name = "Visitor Center",          color = visitor_center_color, type = "point"),
    list(name = "Test Well",               color = test_well_color, type = "point"),
    list(name = "Weather Station",         color = weather_station_color, type = "square"),
    list(name = "Roads",                   color = road_color, type = "line")
  )
  if (!show_visitor_center) legend_items <- Filter(function(i) i$name != "Visitor Center", legend_items)
  if (!show_test_well) legend_items <- Filter(function(i) i$name != "Test Well", legend_items)
  if (!show_weather_station) legend_items <- Filter(function(i) i$name != "Weather Station", legend_items)
  if (!show_roads)     legend_items <- Filter(function(i) i$name != "Roads", legend_items)
  legend_items <- Filter(function(i) !i$name %in% legend_drop, legend_items)

  img <- magick::image_draw(img)
  # image_draw() flips the y axis, so text sizes come back negative
  row_h <- 1.9 * abs(strheight("Mg", cex = cex, font = 2))
  sym_w <- 80 * s; gap <- 20 * s; pad <- 30 * s
  text_w <- max(abs(strwidth(vapply(legend_items, `[[`, "", "name"), cex = cex, font = 2)))
  box_w <- pad + sym_w + gap + text_w + pad
  box_h <- pad + length(legend_items) * row_h + pad
  x1 <- legend_corner[1] * w; y1 <- legend_corner[2] * h
  x0 <- x1 - box_w; y0 <- y1 - box_h
  rect(x0, y0, x1, y1, col = "white", border = "gray20", lwd = 3 * s)
  for (k in seq_along(legend_items)) {
    item <- legend_items[[k]]
    y <- y0 + pad + (k - 0.5) * row_h
    xs <- x0 + pad; xm <- xs + sym_w / 2
    if (item$type == "square") {
      points(xm, y, pch = 22, bg = item$color, col = "white", cex = 3.5 * s, lwd = 2 * s)
    } else if (item$type == "point") {
      points(xm, y, pch = 21, bg = item$color, col = "white", cex = 3.5 * s, lwd = 2 * s)
    } else if (item$type == "line") {
      segments(xs, y, xs + sym_w, y, col = item$color, lwd = 7 * s)
    } else {
      rect(xs, y - 0.3 * row_h, xs + sym_w, y + 0.3 * row_h, col = item$color, border = NA)
    }
    text(xs + sym_w + gap, y, item$name, adj = c(0, 0.5), cex = cex, font = 2, col = "gray15")
  }
  dev.off()

  # Notes strip below the render, wrapped to the image width
  notes <- c(paste0("Vertical exaggeration ", z_exag, "x."), credit)
  strip <- magick::image_blank(w, round(h / 2), "white") %>% magick::image_draw()
  line_h <- 1.5 * abs(strheight("Mg", cex = cex))
  chars <- floor((w - 120 * s) / abs(strwidth("n", cex = cex)))
  lines <- unlist(lapply(notes, strwrap, width = chars))
  text(60 * s, 30 * s + (seq_along(lines) - 0.5) * line_h, lines,
       adj = c(0, 0.5), cex = cex, col = "gray25")
  dev.off()
  strip <- magick::image_crop(strip, paste0(w, "x", round(60 * s + length(lines) * line_h), "+0+0"))

  magick::image_append(c(img, strip), stack = TRUE) %>%
    magick::image_write(png_out)
  png_out
}


get_nps_texture <- function(dem, dem_crs, style = "standard", zoom = 16) {
  # 1. Create an sf bounding box from the DEM in geographic coordinates for the helper
  dem_poly <- sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(dem)) %>%
    sf::st_transform(4326)
  
  # 2. Fetch the NPS basemap tiles (returns Web Mercator SpatRaster)
  tiles_mercator <- get_nps_basemap(dem_poly, style = style, buffer_km = 0, zoom = zoom)
  
  # 3. Reproject and resample the tiles to match your exact local DEM grid and CRS
  tiles_proj <- terra::project(tiles_mercator, dem, method = "bilinear")
  
  # 4. Convert to an RGB array in [0, 1] for rayshader
  arr <- terra::as.array(tiles_proj[[1:3]]) / 255
  arr[is.na(arr)] <- 0
  pmin(pmax(arr, 0), 1)
}

```

# 4. Basin view from the lidar DTM

Crop the lidar to the Blowhard catchment plus a buffer, convert elevations
to the horizontal unit (both are US ft, so no conversion is needed), and
aggregate for rendering.


```{r basin_dem}

# 1. Safely check projection from CRS string
crs_str <- terra::crs(dem)
is_proj <- !grepl("GEOGCRS|Geographic|latlong|longlat", crs_str, ignore.case = TRUE)

# 2. Buffer the park boundary appropriately
if (is_proj) {
  is_meters <- grepl("metre|meter", crs_str, ignore.case = TRUE)
  effective_buffer <- if (is_meters) aoi_buffer_ft * 0.3048 else aoi_buffer_ft
} else {
  effective_buffer <- aoi_buffer_ft * 0.3048 / 111320 
}

aoi <- park_boundary %>%
  sf::st_union() %>%
  sf::st_buffer(aoi_buffer_ft) %>%
  sf::st_bbox()

# 3. Crop and force values into memory
dem_basin <- dem %>%
  terra::crop(terra::ext(aoi[["xmin"]], aoi[["xmax"]], aoi[["ymin"]], aoi[["ymax"]]))

# Verify the crop didn't result in an empty raster
if (terra::ncell(dem_basin) == 0) {
  stop("Error: The bounding box crop resulted in 0 cells. Check that park_boundary and dem share the same coordinate reference system!")
}

dem_basin <- terra::aggregate(dem_basin, fact = dem_agg, fun = "mean", na.rm = TRUE)

# 4. Cell size and elevation scaling
cell_size <- terra::res(dem_basin)[1]
zscale_true <- cell_size
zscale_plot <- cell_size / z_exag

# Convert to matrix safely
elmat_basin <- raster_to_matrix(dem_basin)

# Verify dimensions and range
print(dim(elmat_basin))
print(range(elmat_basin, na.rm = TRUE))

```


```{r spring_band}

# Define your target spring emergence elevation range (in meters)
spring_min_elev <- 2450
spring_max_elev <- 2600

# Create a reclassification matrix: values inside range become 1, others NA
rcl_mat <- matrix(c(
  -Inf,           spring_min_elev, NA,
  spring_min_elev, spring_max_elev, 1,
  spring_max_elev, Inf,            NA
), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

# Mask the basin DEM to that elevation range
elev_mask <- terra::classify(dem_basin, rcl = rcl_mat)

# Convert the mask raster to an sf polygon object and match CRS
spring_band_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(terra::as.polygons(elev_mask, dissolve = TRUE)) %>%
  sf::st_transform(dem_crs)

```

                           zscale = zscale_true, zoom = imagery_zoom) %>%
  add_catchments(elmat_basin, extent = as.vector(terra::ext(dem_basin)))


# Flat map of the same texture, useful for checking overlays

```{r basin_render}

preview <- FALSE

# Scale bar, drawn on the terrain along one edge of the model ("N", "S", "E",
# or "W") and true to scale where it is drawn.
# Put it on an edge facing the camera: with cam_basin theta = -145, north is
# toward the lower right of the image, so the N edge is in front.
scalebar_km       <- 5
scalebar_position <- "N"
scalebar_start    <- 0.10   # where the bar starts along that edge (fraction)
scalebar_inset    <- 0.01   # how far in from the edge the bar sits (fraction)
# Nudge the drawn bar on the image (fraction of image width, height; +x right,
# +y down), e.g. c(0.03, 0.05) to move it off the block onto the white
# background. Length and angle stay as measured on the terrain.
scalebar_shift    <- c(-.1, 0.05)

# North arrow, drawn on the image and rotated to where north points in this
# view. Position is a fraction of the image width / height from the top left.
north_arrow_x <- 0.1
north_arrow_y <- 0.7

cam_basin <- list(theta = -145, phi = 50, zoom = 0.85, fov = 20)

rgl::close3d()
plot_3d(tex_basin, elmat_basin,
        zscale = zscale_plot,
        solid = TRUE, soliddepth = "auto", solidcolor = "gray25",
        solidlinecolor = "gray25",
        shadow = TRUE, shadowdepth = "auto", shadowcolor = "gray45",
        background = "white",
        windowsize = c(out_width, out_height) / 2)

render_camera(theta = cam_basin$theta, phi = cam_basin$phi,
              zoom = cam_basin$zoom, fov = cam_basin$fov)

# North arrow direction: project a south-north pair of ground points into the
# image (drawn later by add_north_arrow()). The DEM grid is UTM, so grid north
# is ~true north.
north_px <- project_to_image(north_ground_points(dem_basin), dem_basin, zscale_plot)

# The scale bar is drawn on the rendered image by add_scalebar() (helpers),
# along the terrain near the `scalebar_position` edge. rayshader's
# render_scalebar() sits at the base of the block and its labels aren't legible.
scalebar_pts <- scalebar_ground_points(dem_basin)
scalebar_px  <- dplyr::bind_cols(sf::st_drop_geometry(scalebar_pts),
                                 project_to_image(scalebar_pts, dem_basin, zscale_plot))

# 1. Project Blowhard Intake Point
intake_target <- current_intake %>%
  dplyr::mutate(system = "Blowhard Intake")
intake_coords <- project_to_image(intake_target, dem_basin, zscale_plot)
target_intake_df <- dplyr::bind_cols(sf::st_drop_geometry(intake_target), intake_coords)

# 2. Sample and project point along Park Boundary
park_boundary_pts <- sf::st_line_sample(
  sf::st_cast(sf::st_boundary(park_boundary), "LINESTRING", warn = FALSE), 
  density = 1 / 500
) %>% 
  sf::st_cast("POINT") %>%
  sf::st_sf(geometry = .) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(system = "Cedar Breaks Boundary")

park_coords <- project_to_image(park_boundary_pts, dem_basin, zscale_plot)
target_park_df <- dplyr::bind_cols(sf::st_drop_geometry(park_boundary_pts), park_coords)

# 3. Project the visitor center
vc_coords <- project_to_image(visitor_center, dem_basin, zscale_plot)
target_vc_df <- dplyr::bind_cols(sf::st_drop_geometry(visitor_center), vc_coords)

# 4. Project the test well and weather station
target_well_df <- dplyr::bind_cols(sf::st_drop_geometry(test_well),
                                   project_to_image(test_well, dem_basin, zscale_plot))
target_station_df <- dplyr::bind_cols(sf::st_drop_geometry(blowhard_station),
                                      project_to_image(blowhard_station, dem_basin, zscale_plot))

# Combine target points for callouts
basin_targets <- dplyr::bind_rows(target_intake_df, target_park_df, target_vc_df,
                                  if (show_test_well) target_well_df,
                                  if (show_weather_station) target_station_df)

basin_raw <- file.path(fig_dir, paste0("catchment_3d_basin_", drape, "_raw.png"))
basin_callout_png <- file.path(fig_dir, paste0("catchment_3d_basin_", drape, "_callouts.png"))

map_credit <- paste0("Elevation: USGS 3D Elevation Program (via elevatr). ",
  if (show_roads) "Roads: OpenStreetMap contributors. " else "",
  if (drape == "imagery") "Imagery: Esri World Imagery."
  else "Shaded relief from the elevation model.")

if (preview) {
  # A low-sample path-traced render at half size, so the preview matches the
  # lighting of the final figure.
  preview_png <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
  render_highquality(filename = preview_png, samples = 16,
                     width = out_width / 2, height = out_height / 2,
                     lightdirection = c(225, 45), lightaltitude = c(55, 60),
                     lightintensity = c(700, 250), lightcolor = c("white", "white"),
                     interactive = FALSE, preview = FALSE)
  add_callouts(preview_png, preview_png, basin_targets)
  add_scalebar(preview_png, preview_png, scalebar_px)
  add_north_arrow(preview_png, preview_png, north_px)
  if (show_elevation_bar && drape == "hillshade") {
    add_elevation_bar(preview_png, preview_png, range(elmat_basin, na.rm = TRUE))
  }
  add_legend(preview_png, preview_png, credit = map_credit)
  plot(magick::image_read(preview_png))
} else {
  render_highquality(filename = basin_raw,
                     samples = hq_samples,
                     width = out_width, height = out_height,
                     lightdirection = c(225, 45), lightaltitude = c(55,60),
                     lightintensity = c(700, 250), lightcolor = c("white", "white"),
                     interactive = FALSE, preview = FALSE)

  add_callouts(basin_raw, basin_callout_png, basin_targets)
  add_scalebar(basin_callout_png, basin_callout_png, scalebar_px)
  add_north_arrow(basin_callout_png, basin_callout_png, north_px)
  if (show_elevation_bar && drape == "hillshade") {
    add_elevation_bar(basin_callout_png, basin_callout_png, range(elmat_basin, na.rm = TRUE))
  }
  add_legend(basin_callout_png,
             file.path(fig_dir, paste0("catchment_3d_basin_", drape, ".png")),
             credit = map_credit)
}
```


# 6. Orbit animation (optional)

An orbit around the basin view for presentations. `render_movie()` captures the
rgl window, so it needs an interactive session with XQuartz.

```{r basin_movie, eval = FALSE}

plot_3d(tex_basin, elmat_basin, zscale = zscale_plot,
        solid = TRUE, shadow = TRUE, background = "white",
        windowsize = c(1400, 950))
render_movie(filename = file.path(fig_dir, "catchment_3d_basin_orbit.mp4"),
             type = "orbit", frames = 360, fps = 30,
             phi = cam_basin$phi, zoom = cam_basin$zoom, fov = cam_basin$fov)

```
